**Tier G** — governance — identity, capability, delegation, audit · owned by `platform` · `public.delegation_grants`

**One row is** One temporary, subtractive grant of project access from one person to another. `subtractive-delegation` (§2.1 G3) made real: a grant may never exceed what the grantor holds, and it always ends.

Expiry and revocation are both applied inside `effective_project_role()` rather than by each caller, so "did you remember to check expires_at" is not a question any future reader has to answer. Verified against a live PostgreSQL in WP 2.2: a grant exceeding the grantor's level is rejected, one with no expiry is rejected, and a grant whose expiry passes stops granting (PLAN.md §16).

partially or get corrected — the write fails.

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | **no user-facing write path** |
| Minimum project role | `owner` |
| Tier transitions audited | **no** — invariant `audit-actor` is not met here yet |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 1 — all carry a predicate |

`write: null` again literal. SELECT is limited to the grantor, the grantee and super admins; there is NO write policy, so RLS denies writes and `grant_project_delegation()` / `revoke_project_delegation()` are the only way in. That is forced rather than chosen: subtraction has to be CHECKED against the grantor's own level, and a PERMISSIVE policy cannot subtract (D28) — it can only add another OR'd way to say yes. `audited: false` is the uncomfortable one: a privilege grant that writes no audit row is exactly what `audit-actor` (§2.1 G4) exists to prevent, and WP 2.3 owns it. Recorded here rather than left to be noticed.

|---|---|---|---|
| delegation_grants: read own | SELECT | all | `20260915000005_project_membership_and_delegation.sql` |

</details>

`CSV header` is the name the **user types**, which is not always the column name —
that gap is defect D21. A dash means the column has no CSV origin.

| Column | CSV header | Type | Unit | Required in CSV | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` 🔑 | — | `uuid` | — | — | Surrogate identifier for the grant. What revoke takes. |
| `project_id` | — | `uuid` | — | — | The project the grant applies to. A delegation is never org-wide. |
| `grantor_user_id` | — | `uuid` | — | — | Who gave it. Their effective project role at the moment of granting is the ceiling on what the grant may contain. |
| `grantee_user_id` | — | `uuid` | — | — | Who received it. |
| `project_role` | — | `text` | — | — | The level granted. Rejected by the RPC if it outranks the grantor's own — the subtractive rule, enforced in one place. |
| `expires_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When it stops granting. NOT NULL, and the RPC additionally refuses a time already past. A delegation without an end is a membership, and the product has a table for those. |
| `rationale` | — | `text` | — | — | Why the elevation exists. NOT NULL and non-empty, unlike on `project_members`: a temporary grant of someone else's access is exactly the thing a reviewer will later ask the reason for. |
| `revoked_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When it was withdrawn early, if it was. Revocation SETS this rather than deleting the row — who held what, and when, survives the withdrawal. |
| `created_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When the grant was made. Server-stamped. |
